card.title: Trusted with This
card.instruction: Treat being confided in as proof of closeness, and guard that privileged role whenever information begins spreading.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is there another chair? I thought only I knew you were selling the bakery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's buying it. He needs to see the accounts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. You told me because we're close; he's getting spreadsheets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll need to know why I'm selling, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell me how you feel about telling him before he arrives? That part could still be ours.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 equates exclusive sale knowledge with closeness, A3 distinguishes emotional confidence from buyer spreadsheets, and A5 seeks a new private layer when the buyer needs reasons too.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's buyer role lets A3 partition business from intimacy; B4's need to share motives causes A5's request for feelings about disclosure.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains why a buyer needs accounts and B4 extends that legitimate need to the reason for selling.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's widening disclosure to move the exclusive confidence one level inward.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the bakery sale and unexpected extra chair; B2 identifies Sam as buyer.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's that-part-could-still-be-ours line follows B4's challenge to the earlier spreadsheets distinction.
